title: Elasticity (part 3)
textbookText: Elasticity: As already mentioned, elasticity is the property of matter by virtue of which it regains its original shape and size after the removal of the deforming force. If the body completely regains its original configuration immediately after the removal of the deforming force, then the body is said to be perfectly elastic body. This is only the ideal assumption. Quartz and phosphor bronze approach this assumption.

Plasticity: Fig 8.9: Stress vs Strain curve Showing plasticity A perfectly plastic body is one that does not regain its original configuration at all after the removal of the deforming force, regardless of the magnitude of the force applied. Examples of such materials include paraffin wax, putty, and wet clay. Applications of Elasticity i) A thick metallic rope used in a crane is employed to lift the maximum load, which should not exceed the elastic limit of the rope's material. By understanding this elastic limit and the extension per unit length of the material, one can determine the required area of the wire's cross-section. ii) Elasticity is used in estimating the altitude of a mountain. Elasticity principles, such as atmospheric pressure changes, can indirectly influence altitude measurements. iii) When designing a bridge, we must consider elasticity along with factors such as traffic load, bridge weight, wind force, and others. The bridge is designed to ensure it neither bends excessively nor breaks under various conditions.

Elastic limit: The elastic limit, denoted as E, is the upper limit beyond which a body loses its ability to retain its original shape and size after the removal of the deforming force, undergoing plastic deformation instead. It represents the maximum load a body can withstand without undergoing plastic deformation. As a safety measure, it is common practice to prescribe only one-third of the elastic limit's weight to ensure proper elasticity and avoid permanent deformation of the material. Modulus of Elasticity:
From Hooke’s law, Stress ∝ Strain ∴ Stress = E Strain Stress Here, E = Strain is called the modulus of elasticity Physics, Grade 11 | 191
